note:
v1 83.063/79.892. THE MAST, the opener: crescendo post-rock (~9.4 min, 140 bpm, half time first). A radio voice from a mast's night service, and a five-note theme (F#4 E4 D4 A3 B3) transformed through six movements:
I CARRIER: wind, shortwave static and a tuning whistle; the announcer (chirp's voice engine speaking ARPAbet through a radio band-pass): "This is the night service. All the lights are left on. Keep your radio on." The theme on one delayed guitar.
II BRUSHES: brush kit, fretless, an arpeggio; a second guitar answers on new chords; then it thins.
III SNOWFALL: no drums. Celesta plays the theme at half speed over a cello. "Snow on the line. We are still here." The wind rises.
IV CLIMB: the theme in triplets, tremolo guitars whose drive opens bar by bar, toms to sticks to the full kit, strings swelling, a violin counter-melody.
V THE LIGHTS: the key lifts a tone on the peak's downbeat. A crash-ride wash, a driven wall and an 8-string under it, the theme in long values on a tape-echo lead with glockenspiel, a sub pumped by the kick.
VI STILL ON: piano and static; the voice slowed and lowered: "All the lights are left on." The theme's first three notes, and no ending.
Dynamic true-peak master with a fader ride per movement: rms -17.8 dB, crest 13.2 dB, TP -1.19 dBTP, no flat runs.
The metric undersells post-rock: a slow crescendo reads as recurrence (share 0.81 is past the band's 0.7) and straight time reads as low rhythm (off-grid 0.01). I propose album measures for that on caco. (Not queued.)

note:
v2 86.742/85.921 (v1 re-scored like for like: 83.029; the seed spread closes from 3.2 to 0.8). True variety where v1 only grew:
- THE TREMOLO IN TRIPLETS: the climb's and the peak's tremolo guitars pick in sextuplets, so the whole climb lives in the triplet feel its theme set up.
- THE FALSE SUMMIT: at the end of the climb's second phase the band cuts away for four bars. The strings play alone and the radio cuts through ("Keep your radio on."), then the climb resumes harder.
- THE LIGHTS FLICKER: half-way through the peak the wall and the kit drop out for eight bars. A half-time kick and the sub hold, the mains HUM swells and RELAYS click, as if the town's lights were failing, and the theme sounds slowed on a far glockenspiel. Then the peak returns with a CHOIR singing the theme at half speed against the lead.
- THE BEACON: the mast's red light, a slow ping every two bars, in the carrier and in the coda.
Recurrence 48 -> 76. Levels: -13.8 LUFS, TP -1.19 dBTP, run 1. T1_R2=none reproduces v1. (Not queued.)
next: Rhythm (55.8) is the straight-time measure; the album measures proposal is still open.
